logback-core is present and used only for console logging in LDAP Gateway 4.1.0; Janino is not on the classpath and logback conditional configuration (<if condition="...">) is not used, so the conditions required for this CVE are not met and it is not believed to be exploitable in this product.

commons-lang3 is present and used by LDAP Gateway 4.1.0, but the vulnerable ClassUtils.getClass(...) API is not referenced in gateway code; we treat this as a library-level CVE with no identified direct usage in the product and will remediate by upgrading to the fixed version.

spring-webmvc is present on the classpath for LDAP Gateway 4.1.0, but the gateway does not define any Spring MVC controllers or reference org.springframework.web.* in its own classes, so the module is effectively unused by product code and the CVE is scoped to an unused framework component.

spring-core 6.2.8 is a core Spring framework dependency used throughout LDAP Gateway 4.1.0 (bean/context wiring in multiple com.pingidentity.lightning.ldapaccess.* classes), so this CVE is treated as a true-positive framework vulnerability and will be remediated by upgrading Spring Core to the fixed version in the next release.

Vulnerable qsort code is present in musl. On 64-bit aarch64 systems, triggering the bug requires arrays exceeding ~34 trillion elements (the 64th Leonardo number), which we do not believe is achievable in typical LDAP Gateway container deployments. Based on this, we do not consider LDAP Gateway deployments to be practically exploitable by this issue.
